# Cover Letter  {#cover-letter}

**Date:** 12th August, 2026

**To**  
 The Procurement Committee  
 World Health Organization (WHO)

**Subject: Proposal Submission – Development of the Health Accounts Data System (HADS), built upon WHO’s existing xMart data warehouse (Reference: PFD-2026-001)** 

Dear Sir/Madam,

Argusoft India Limited is pleased to submit its Technical and Financial Proposal for the **Development of the Health Accounts Data System (HADS), built upon WHO’s existing xMart data warehouse**. We appreciate the opportunity to partner with the World Health Organization (WHO) in delivering a secure, scalable, and configurable platform that strengthens the collection, validation, management, and analysis of National Health Accounts data across Member States.

We recognize that National Health Accounts are fundamental to evidence-based health financing and health system governance. Reliable Health Accounts data enables governments to monitor health expenditure, evaluate financing reforms, support Universal Health Coverage (UHC), and make informed policy decisions. Through this initiative, WHO is modernizing its digital ecosystem to improve data quality, standardization, collaboration, and analytical capabilities. We are committed to delivering a sustainable platform that contributes to stronger national health information systems and better health financing decisions worldwide.

For over **25 years**, Argusoft has been delivering enterprise digital transformation solutions for governments, international organizations, and public sector institutions. Our expertise includes configurable enterprise platforms, metadata-driven applications, workflow automation, analytics, cloud-native architectures, secure software engineering, interoperability, and long-term application support.

Argusoft has built a strong partnership with the **World Health Organization** through the successful delivery and ongoing support of several strategic digital platforms. Our WHO portfolio includes the **Joint External Evaluation (JEE) Reporting Platform**, **Early Warning, Alert and Response System (EWARS)**, **Event Management Suite (EMS2)**, **Simulation Exercise (SimEx)**, **WHO Emergency Public Dashboard**, and the **P4H World Platform**, which supports global collaboration on social health protection and health financing. These engagements have provided us with a deep understanding of WHO's digital ecosystem, delivery standards, cybersecurity requirements, and collaborative implementation approach.

Equally important, Argusoft has extensive experience implementing **national-scale Health Information Systems**, directly aligning with the objectives of this assignment. Our portfolio includes **TeCHO+**, serving over **65 million citizens** through **13,500+ health workers** in Gujarat; **eKavach**, supporting more than **300 million beneficiaries** through **180,000+ field health workers** in Uttar Pradesh; **ImpactHealth Nigeria**; **EmCare (Clinical Care in Crisis)** developed with WHO; and **P-HMMS** for HIV programme management. These platforms demonstrate our expertise in developing configurable, metadata-driven health information systems with complex workflows, data validation, reporting, interoperability, mobile applications, and large-scale data management.

Our broader experience includes delivering enterprise platforms for governments and international organizations such as the **License Management System** for the Government of Jamaica, the **Data Visualization and Business Intelligence Platform**, **Trust and Estate Management System**, **Jamaica Customs Portal**, and **Boston College EagleApps**. These engagements demonstrate our capability to deliver enterprise applications involving configurable workflows, document management, analytics, dashboards, API integrations, and secure cloud deployments.

Having reviewed the Terms of Reference and technical requirements, we understand that the solution will leverage **xMart’s existing capabilities** while extending the ecosystem to support Health Accounts-specific processes. Argusoft’s direct experience integrating the WHO Emergency Public Dashboard with xMart, together with our end-to-end experience delivering applications within WHO’s Azure environment and our expertise in configurable enterprise platforms, workflow engines, metadata-driven applications, validation frameworks, and analytics solutions, positions us well to deliver a scalable, maintainable, and sustainable HADS solution. 

Our implementation approach combines collaborative requirements validation, agile delivery, rigorous quality assurance, comprehensive documentation, structured knowledge transfer, and user training. We are committed to working closely with WHO throughout the project lifecycle to deliver a secure, user-centric, and future-ready solution that meets the highest standards of quality and performance.

We confirm that we have carefully reviewed the Request for Proposal, its Terms of Reference, and the accompanying annexes, and that our proposal has been prepared in accordance with the stated requirements and the applicable Long-Term Agreement. We are confident that our extensive WHO experience, proven track record in national health information systems, and expertise in configurable enterprise platforms strongly position Argusoft to successfully deliver the Health Accounts Data System on the xMart Platform.

We thank you for considering our proposal and look forward to the opportunity to partner with the World Health Organization on this important initiative.

Yours faithfully,

# Executive Summary {#executive-summary}

The World Health Organization (WHO) is undertaking the modernization of its **Health Accounts Data Management System (DMS)** to replace the current legacy application with a centralized, web-based platform built on the existing **xMart** platform. The new DMS will support the collection, storage, consolidation, validation, analysis, and publication of National Health Accounts data while improving system performance, strengthening quality checks, supporting report production, and enabling seamless integration with WHO's Health Accounts ecosystem, including xMart, HAPT, eDamis, the Global Health Expenditure Database (GHED), and other data sources.

Argusoft India Limited proposes a configurable, secure, and scalable Data Management System that leverages the existing capabilities of the xMart platform while implementing the functional, technical, and integration requirements defined by WHO. The proposed solution will provide a centralized environment for managing Health Accounts data, metadata, formulas, workbooks, reports, quality checks, and version-controlled information through configurable modules and standards-based APIs. In line with the proposed target architecture, xMart will continue to serve as the primary Health Accounts data warehouse, while the DMS will provide the business functionality and user interface required for data management and analysis.

Argusoft is particularly well positioned for this assignment through its direct, hands-on experience with WHO’s xMart platform. For the WHO Emergency Public Dashboard, our team integrated the application with the secured xMart OData API to retrieve and process data from xMart tables and views for dashboards, reports, and analytics. The team also used xMart’s Excel-based model upload capability to define and update custom data models. Combined with our end-to-end experience delivering and supporting applications within WHO’s Azure environment, this provides Argusoft with practical familiarity with WHO’s integration patterns, accessibility expectations, cybersecurity requirements, deployment processes, release governance, and operational standards. This existing knowledge will reduce onboarding, integration, security-review, and deployment risks and support accelerated delivery of the Pilot and subsequent phases. 

Our solution is designed to support the complete business processes defined within the Requirements Document, including user and role management, metadata and configuration management, workbook management, reporting, data and metadata versioning, configurable quality checks, xMart integration, and phased implementation. The solution will support controlled two-way data exchange with xMart, including retrieval of the required Health Accounts data, metadata, formulas, version information, and configuration through xMart’s secured OData API, and transmission of DMS-generated updates through the applicable WHO-approved xMart data-ingestion mechanism. This approach will maintain consistency between the DMS and xMart while aligning with WHO’s prescribed integration architecture. 

Recognizing that the success of this assignment depends not only on technology but also on an effective delivery methodology, Argusoft proposes a hybrid implementation approach combining the strengths of both Waterfall and Agile methodologies. The initial phases will follow a structured approach focused on project initiation, requirements validation, business process analysis, solution architecture, and interactive prototype development to establish a common understanding of the proposed solution. Following design approval, development will transition to iterative Agile delivery through two-to-three-week sprints, enabling incremental delivery of prioritized functionalities, regular demonstrations, stakeholder feedback, and progressive validation. Sprint deliverables will first be deployed to the UAT environment for WHO review and acceptance before approved releases are promoted to Production, with identified defects addressed within the current or following sprint. This approach provides clarity during solution definition while maintaining the flexibility required to support WHO’s phased implementation model. 

The proposed implementation covers the complete project lifecycle, including solution design, development of the Pilot functionalities, incremental implementation of subsequent functionalities, quality assurance, testing, deployment to User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and Production environments, integration with WHO systems, legacy data and formula migration, documentation, administrator and end-user training, source code handover, and cloud infrastructure support and maintenance in accordance with the Terms of Reference.

The proposed solution provides the following key capabilities:

* Centralized, web-based Data Management System built upon WHO’s existing xMart data warehouse.   
* Configurable management of users, roles, metadata, formulas, workbooks, reports, and quality check rules.  
* Controlled two-way integration with xMart for the retrieval and synchronization of data, metadata, formulas, version information, and configuration through WHO-approved integration mechanisms.   
* Support for Health Accounts data collection, validation, consolidation, reporting, and publication.  
* Data and metadata versioning, comparison, restoration, auditability, and configurable quality checks.  
* Phased implementation beginning with Pilot functionalities followed by incremental delivery of the remaining requirements.  
* Secure cloud deployment, comprehensive documentation, knowledge transfer, user training, and post-implementation support.

By combining a configurable platform architecture, a structured hybrid delivery methodology, and a collaborative implementation approach, Argusoft will deliver a sustainable Health Accounts Data Management System that aligns with WHO's functional and technical requirements while providing a scalable foundation for future enhancements and continued support of the Health Accounts programme.

# Relevant Experience  (Past Project References)  {#relevant-experience-(past-project-references)}

Argusoft brings over 25 years of experience in designing, developing, deploying, and supporting **large-scale enterprise data management platforms, digital health information systems, and workflow-driven applications** for the World Health Organization (WHO), international organizations, governments, and public-sector institutions. Our portfolio includes mission-critical systems supporting disease surveillance, emergency response, health financing, clinical decision support, analytics, and national public health programmes.

Of particular relevance to this assignment, Argusoft has direct, **hands-on experience with WHO’s xMart platform** through the development and ongoing support of the WHO Emergency Public Dashboard. The Argusoft team integrated the application with the **secured xMart OData API** to retrieve and process data from xMart tables and views for dashboards, reports and analytics. The team also used **xMart’s Excel-based model upload capability** to define and update custom data models within the applicable mart. This work provided practical experience with xMart mart structures, tables and views, OData query patterns, filtering, authentication, model configuration and downstream data consumption—capabilities directly relevant to the proposed Health Accounts DMS. 

Argusoft also has proven experience delivering WHO applications through the **complete software development lifecycle within WHO’s Azure environment**. For applications including the **JEE Reporting Platform, eNAPHS and EWARS**, Argusoft has been responsible for requirements analysis, solution design, application development, testing, security remediation, deployment to WHO Azure environments, production release, documentation, training, maintenance, and ongoing technical support. Through these engagements, our teams have developed practical familiarity with **WHO’s accessibility expectations, including applicable WCAG requirements; cybersecurity and application-security requirements; Azure deployment and release processes; technical documentation standards; quality assurance practices; and operational governance procedures**.

This combination of **existing xMart integration experience, end-to-end WHO Azure delivery experience, and long-term support of mission-critical WHO platforms** provides Argusoft with a significant advantage for this assignment. Our team will begin with established knowledge of WHO’s technology and governance environment, thereby reducing onboarding time, avoiding preventable integration and deployment issues, and accelerating delivery of the Pilot and subsequent phases.

Our broader experience encompasses the complete lifecycle of enterprise application delivery, including business analysis, requirements engineering, solution architecture, UI/UX design, application development, API integration, cloud deployment, legacy system modernization, data and metadata migration, testing, training, knowledge transfer, warranty services, and long-term maintenance. We have successfully developed platforms that manage complex and multidimensional datasets, configurable workflows, validation rules, metadata, reporting and analytics, and interoperability across enterprise systems.

Across the selected projects, Argusoft demonstrates:

* **Direct experience with WHO xMart**, including OData-based API integration and the use of the xMart Model Uploader for onboarding custom data models and associated data.  
* **End-to-end delivery within WHO’s Azure environment**, covering development, testing, deployment, production release, monitoring, maintenance, and technical support.  
* Practical understanding of **WHO accessibility, cybersecurity, quality assurance, deployment, documentation, and governance requirements**.  
* Proven delivery and long-term support of **mission-critical WHO digital platforms**.  
* Extensive experience developing **health information systems, enterprise data management platforms, and workflow-driven applications**.  
* Strong capability in **metadata-driven solution design, data validation, workflow automation, reporting, dashboards, and analytics**.  
* Experience integrating multiple systems through **OData, REST APIs, and standards-based interoperability mechanisms**.  
* Successful modernization of **legacy enterprise applications** into scalable, secure, and maintainable web-based platforms.  
* Proven capability in **training, knowledge transfer, warranty services, and long-term operational support**.

### 5\. iFile Teapot

 **Client Name:** IRIS RegTech Solutions Limited  
**Implementation Period \-** 2024 \- Ongoing  
**Country region/ Scale** : **India, Malaysia and Qatar**, with clients including **GTA, PFRDA and QCB**, and supports **more than 100,000 users**  
**Project Status:** Ongoing   
**Contract Value**\- USD 500k \+  
**Argusoft's Role:**Development, hosting, maintenance, enhancements, support, data management, documentation and training.

**Project Description:**  
 IRIS iFile is a comprehensive, end-to-end electronic filing and regulatory reporting platform designed for structured data collection, validation, submission, processing, storage and analysis by regulators and regulated entities. The platform supports financial, statistical, compliance-related and other structured data and is built around internationally recognized XBRL and SDMX standards for machine-readable data exchange. IRIS states that iFile is trusted by 30+ regulators worldwide and has processed millions of filings globally, demonstrating its use in large-scale regulatory data environments.

The iFile platform provides an end-to-end regulatory data lifecycle covering **data modelling, data dictionaries and relationships, taxonomy and business rules, data collection, form generation, automated validation, workflow management, processing, reporting, analytics and data dissemination**. It supports both system-to-system and screen-based submissions, allowing regulators to collect data from entities with different levels of technical capability. The platform uses a flexible component-based architecture and is available on **Microsoft and Java technology stacks**, with a microservices-based architecture and **BPMN workflow engine**.

The iFile Teapot implementation includes **return submissions through multiple channels, including screen submission and webform upload; multiple return types; BPMN-based maker-checker workflows; DynaForms for drag-and-drop form creation; a renderer engine for generated forms; Bushchat integration; MIS reporting; and metadata validation of XML**. The implementation currently covers **India, Malaysia and Qatar**, with clients including **GTA, PFRDA and QCB**, and supports **more than 100,000 users with approximately 2,000–3,000 concurrent users**. The technology stack used for the implementation includes **Angular 20, Java, Node.js for the BPMN engine, NestJS for DynaForms and PostgreSQL**.

The broader iFile platform is designed for demanding financial and regulatory environments, including **central banks, pension regulators, capital-market regulators, business registries, insurance and other financial-sector regulators**. The platform supports **automated business-rule validation of more than 2,000 rules per data point**, handles filings/data of up to **1 GB**, and provides integrated analytics, standard reports, MIS reports, dashboards and statistical reports.

**Project Name:** zValuate – Financial Analysis and Data Processing Platform  
**Implementation Period:** August 2022 to Ongoing

**Argusoft's Role:** Development of a web-based financial analysis and data-processing platform enabling users to define visual workflows, manage financial datasets, perform data merges and transformations, configure calculations, maintain workflow and dataset versions, generate outputs and maintain a complete audit trail linking source data, processing logic and resulting outputs. 

**Project Description**

zValuate is a **financial analysis and data-processing platform** designed to maintain an auditable relationship between input data, processing logic, calculations and resulting outputs. The platform enables users to create workflow models for financial operations through a web-based visual interface, allowing multiple datasets and individual data fields to be processed through configurable data blocks, merges, transformations and calculation blocks. Workflow metadata records the purpose, author, creation date, constituent blocks, operations and connections, while changes to workflows and input/output datasets are maintained as versions. This allows users to reconstruct how a particular financial result was produced and identify the source datasets and processing logic associated with the result. # Technical Proposal / Methodology Proposed in the Proposal {#technical-proposal-/-methodology-proposed-in-the-proposal}

## Scope of Work \- Our Understanding  {#scope-of-work---our-understanding}

### Background

The World Health Organization (WHO) is undertaking a strategic initiative to modernize its **Health Accounts Data Management System (DMS)** by replacing the existing legacy application that currently supports the collection, storage, consolidation, validation, analysis, and publication of National Health Accounts data. As the volume and complexity of Health Accounts data continue to grow, there is a need for a modern, scalable, and maintainable platform that improves system performance, strengthens data quality and quality assurance processes, supports multidimensional datasets, and enhances reporting capabilities across Member States.

This initiative forms part of WHO's broader effort to strengthen Health Accounts data management through an integrated digital ecosystem. By modernizing the DMS and improving interoperability with existing Health Accounts systems and data sources, WHO aims to streamline data management processes, improve collaboration across Headquarters, Regional and Country Offices, and support timely, standardized, and evidence-based health financing analysis and reporting.

### Objectives of the RFP

Based on our comprehensive review of the Request for Proposal (RFP), Terms of Reference, Functional Requirements, API Specifications, and Clarifications, we understand that the primary objective of this assignment is to design, develop, deploy, and support a centralized, web-based **Health Accounts Data Management System (DMS)** built upon WHO's existing **xMart** platform. The solution is intended to replace the existing legacy application and provide a configurable, integrated, and sustainable platform for managing the complete lifecycle of National Health Accounts data while strengthening data quality, interoperability, reporting, and operational efficiency.

To achieve this objective, the assignment is expected to fulfil the following:

**1\. Develop a Modern Health Accounts Data Management System**

Design and develop a centralized, web-based DMS that replaces the legacy application and supports the collection, storage, consolidation, validation, analysis, and publication of Health Accounts data through a configurable and user-friendly platform.

**2\. Support the Complete Health Accounts Data Management Lifecycle**

Implement functionalities for user and role management, setup and metadata management, workbook management, reporting, data and metadata versioning, configurable quality checks, notifications, and phased implementation in accordance with the Functional Requirements.

**3\. Enable Seamless Integration with WHO Systems**

Integrate the DMS with the existing **xMart** platform and other WHO systems through secure APIs to support automated data exchange, metadata synchronization, formula management, and interoperability across the Health Accounts ecosystem.

**4\. Improve Data Quality, Validation, and Reporting**

Strengthen the management of multidimensional Health Accounts datasets through configurable quality check rules, version control, reporting, dashboards, and standardized validation processes to improve the reliability and consistency of published Health Accounts information.

**5\. Implement the Solution through a Phased Delivery Approach**

Develop and deploy the Pilot functionalities followed by the incremental implementation of the remaining functional requirements, supported by iterative testing, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), production deployment, and continuous stakeholder validation throughout the project lifecycle.

**6\. Support Deployment, Knowledge Transfer, and Operational Sustainability**

Establish and maintain the UAT and Production environments, provide cloud infrastructure support and maintenance, prepare technical and user documentation, conduct user training, and hand over the complete source code and system artefacts to ensure long-term sustainability of the solution.

### Scope of Work – Our Understanding

Based on our detailed review of the Request for Proposal (RFP), Terms of Reference, Functional Requirements, API Specifications, and clarifications, we understand that the selected Contractor will be responsible for the following key components:

**Solution Design & System Architecture**

Design the overall technical architecture, user interface, database structure, and implementation framework for the new Health Accounts Data Management System (DMS). This includes solution design, prototypes, technical specifications, and implementation planning aligned with the phased delivery approach.

**Development of the Health Accounts Data Management System**

Develop a web-based DMS on the xMart platform, implementing the Pilot functionalities followed by the remaining functional requirements. The system should support user and role management, metadata management, workbook management, reporting, versioning, configurable quality checks, notifications, and administration functions.

**Integration & Data Migration**

Implement secure bidirectional integration between the DMS and xMart through the prescribed APIs. The scope includes the required one-time migration of legacy Health Accounts data and  formulas from the old DMS Microsoft SQL Server into the agreed xMart/DMS target structures, including formula metadata migration and conversion into the new DMS formula syntax as required by UC060. Detailed mappings, reconciliation, validation and cutover will be agreed during discovery. Existing recurring pipelines from external systems into xMart are already in place and are not part of DMS development.

**Data Quality, Reporting & Analytics**

Implement configurable quality checks, reporting, dashboards, data validation, and version management to improve the consistency, traceability, and management of multidimensional Health Accounts datasets.

**Testing, Deployment & Cloud Infrastructure**

Conduct comprehensive testing, support User Acceptance Testing (UAT), deploy the solution to Production, and establish the required cloud infrastructure. The Contractor will also provide infrastructure monitoring and operational support throughout the contract period.

**Documentation, Training & Knowledge Transfer**

Prepare technical and user documentation, conduct administrator and user training, and provide knowledge transfer to ensure successful adoption, operation, and long-term sustainability of the platform.

**Warranty, Support & Maintenance**

Provide warranty support, application maintenance, issue resolution, cloud infrastructure support, monitoring, and regular support services in accordance with the Terms of Reference.

**Ultimate Goal**

The Health Accounts Data Management System is envisioned as a centralized, integrated, and configurable platform that modernizes the management of National Health Accounts data. By replacing the legacy application and leveraging the xMart platform, the new DMS will strengthen data quality, reporting, interoperability, and operational efficiency, while supporting evidence-based health financing analysis and the continued evolution of WHO's Health Accounts programme.

## Approach  {#approach}

Our approach to delivering the **Health Accounts Data Management System (DMS)** is centred on collaboration, configurability, and sustainability. We recognize that the success of this assignment depends not only on replacing the existing legacy application but also on delivering a solution that aligns with WHO's Health Accounts business processes, integrates seamlessly with the existing **xMart** platform, and supports the long-term evolution of the Health Accounts programme.

We will adopt a business-driven approach, working closely with the WHO Health Accounts team throughout the engagement to validate requirements, understand operational processes, and ensure that the solution reflects both current and future business needs. Continuous stakeholder engagement, regular demonstrations, and timely feedback will be integral to our approach, enabling progressive validation and reducing implementation risks.

Our approach emphasizes **configuration over unnecessary customization**, leveraging the capabilities of the existing xMart platform while extending it where required to meet the defined functional requirements. This ensures consistency with WHO's enterprise architecture, simplifies future maintenance, and provides flexibility to accommodate evolving Health Accounts processes without extensive redevelopment.

Quality will be embedded throughout the engagement rather than treated as a standalone activity. We will apply structured quality assurance, code reviews, testing, and validation practices to ensure that every deliverable meets WHO's functional, technical, and operational expectations before progressing to subsequent stages.

Recognizing the importance of Health Accounts data, our approach emphasizes **data integrity, interoperability and business continuity**. Argusoft will perform the required one-time migration of legacy Health Accounts data and formulas from the old DMS, including approximately 70,000 formulas currently stored in its Microsoft SQL Server database. The migration approach will cover extraction, transformation, loading into the agreed xMart/DMS target structures, formula metadata migration, required conversion into executable new-DMS formulas, reconciliation and WHO validation. Existing recurring pipelines from external systems into xMart are already in place and are not part of DMS development.

Finally, we view this assignment as a long-term partnership rather than a software implementation project. Alongside system delivery, we will focus on knowledge transfer, comprehensive documentation, administrator and user training, and collaborative engagement to enable WHO to effectively operate, maintain, and further evolve the Health Accounts Data Management System beyond the project duration.

**Security & Coding Standards**

Security and quality will be embedded throughout the development lifecycle to ensure the Health Accounts Data Management System aligns with WHO's technical and operational requirements. The solution will integrate with **WHO Entra ID** for secure Single Sign-On (SSO) authentication and role-based access control, ensuring users are authenticated and authorized in accordance with their assigned responsibilities.

Security will be treated as a core, cross-cutting deliverable throughout the solution lifecycle. Argusoft’s in-house cybersecurity team includes professionals holding industry-recognized certifications such as the Hack The Box Certified Penetration Testing Specialist (HTB CPTS), CompTIA Security+, and INE eLearnSecurity Junior Penetration Tester (eJPT). The security team will support architecture and threat reviews, security testing, vulnerability assessment, and remediation verification.

Argusoft will apply an OWASP-aligned secure software development lifecycle, including threat modelling during design, secure coding standards, peer code reviews, static application security testing, software composition analysis and dependency scanning, secret scanning, dynamic application security testing, and remediation of identified vulnerabilities before the Production release. The solution will enforce input validation, least-privilege access, country- and role-based authorization, secure API communication, comprehensive audit trails, centralized logging and monitoring, encryption in transit, and encryption at rest through WHO-approved Azure services and configurations.

As an organization, Argusoft maintains an **ISO/IEC 27001 Information Security Management System (ISMS)** and applies established quality management and software development practices across enterprise projects. These practices support the delivery of secure, maintainable, and scalable solutions while aligning with WHO's cloud-based architecture and security expectations.

## Methodology  {#methodology}

We recognize that the success of this assignment depends not only on the technology but also on the methodology adopted for execution. Considering the scope, stakeholder involvement, system integration, and phased implementation requirements, we propose a **hybrid delivery approach** combining both Waterfall and Agile methodologies.

During the initial phases of planning, requirements validation, and solution design, we will follow a **Waterfall approach**. This will enable detailed requirements finalization, process mapping, and development of interactive prototypes, ensuring all stakeholders have a clear and aligned understanding of the solution.

During the development phase, we will transition to an **Agile methodology**, executing the project in **2–3 week sprints**. A prioritized backlog will be maintained, and incremental functionalities will be delivered with regular demonstrations and feedback cycles to ensure continuous alignment and improvement.

This hybrid approach ensures clarity in planning, flexibility in development, and timely delivery while effectively managing risks and stakeholder expectations throughout the project lifecycle. Each phase will include defined review and approval checkpoints with the **WHO Health Accounts team** to ensure alignment, validation, and controlled progression to subsequent stages.

## Proposed Solution {#proposed-solution}

In response to the requirements set out in the Terms of Reference and the Functional Requirements, we propose a centralized, web based Data Management System for Health Accounts, built upon WHO's existing xMart data warehouse. The application will serve as the single working environment for the WHO Health Accounts team and its colleagues in Regional and Country Offices, covering the full working cycle for country health expenditure data: bringing data together, checking it, calculating indicators, resolving quality issues, tracking what each country has reported, and preparing the year's figures for publication. Users will sign in with their WHO account through Entra ID, and external contributors will be supported as guest accounts under the same sign in path. A single API layer will carry every exchange with xMart and with any other WHO system that needs to read from the DMS, and the application will run on WHO Azure infrastructure sized for the year end peak.

One point shapes almost every design decision that follows. The Functional Requirements are explicit that the main data warehouse for Health Accounts data stays in xMart, that the DMS calls the xMart API whenever it needs to display or process data, and that processed results are returned to xMart once they are complete. The same requirement then adds that the DMS is expected to have a local database of its own. We have taken both halves of that literally. Country health expenditure data, its metadata, the configuration behind it and its version history remain in xMart and are never duplicated as a second authoritative copy. The DMS local database holds what belongs to the application rather than to the warehouse: user accounts and permissions, quality check and report definitions, saved user preferences, background job state, edit locks, notifications and the application audit log. This division keeps one source of truth for the figures that eventually reach the Global Health Expenditure Database and the Global Health Observatory, while giving the application the transactional store it needs to stay responsive and to support several people working at once.

The application will be built to perform well even when a request spans a large slice of the warehouse. Expected volumes range from a few dozen rows to a million, and a full quality check run at year end covers every country at once. To keep this comfortable we will combine server side filtering and paging with caching of the reference data that changes rarely, such as country and currency lists, classifications, crosses, metadata field definitions and formula definitions. Redis is our recommended cache for this, with cache entries cleared automatically when the corresponding value is edited in the Setup module. Long running work does not block the screen: full quality check runs, complex report generation and bulk exports are handed to a durable background job queue, and the user is told when the job finishes through an in app notification carrying a link to the result. Within the browser we will apply virtualized rendering, lazy loading of each module and prefetching of the data a user is most likely to open next, so that a workbook opens quickly regardless of how much history sits behind it.

After a careful review of the scope of work, the Functional Requirements and the API specification, we propose an n-tier architecture for this project. The most important characteristic of this approach is the separation of the service and interface layers, which brings ease of maintenance and ease of extension. The pattern allows the application to grow without compromising performance or accuracy, and its service oriented design builds the application from loosely coupled, interoperable services that communicate through formal contracts independent of the underlying platform and programming language. The presentation tier itself is modelled on the MVC architecture.

The MVC pattern suits this project particularly well because the core business rules of Health Accounts work are already documented in detail, which means they can be built, modified or extended in the business layer without touching any other layer. The proposed solution also uses ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) in the model so that the system stays database agnostic, and it places every call to xMart behind a single integration component so that a change to an xMart contract, authentication method or data structure is absorbed in one place rather than across the application.

**Working Prototype**

Rather than describe the proposed system in writing alone, we have built a working prototype of it and made it available for evaluation at [https://whohadms.argusservices.in/](https://whohadms.argusservices.in/). It covers the application shell, the Setup module, the Workbook with its calculation engine, Quality Checks, Reports, versioning, the dashboard and the data retrieval interface, running against a representative Health Accounts dataset. The screenshots throughout this section are taken from it.

We want to be clear about what the prototype represents. It sets out our proposed solution based on our current understanding of the Terms of Reference, the Functional Requirements, the API specification and the clarifications issued. It is not the delivered product, and the screens shown in this section are not a final design. During the requirements finalization phase we will hold detailed workshops with the WHO Health Accounts team, study the existing DMS and the way the team works with it today, and build a precise understanding of the outcomes expected from the new system. The prototype will then be updated to reflect that input, and the resulting design will be submitted for WHO's review and approval before development begins, as set out in our work plan.

Every part of it, including the navigation, the workbook layout, the report builder and the content of the dashboard, is a proposal open to revision, and we expect it to change once the team has spent time with it.

**Architecture Diagram**

*Solution architecture.*

***The app architecture will have the following layers:*** 

### Front-end (Presentation Layer/Tier)

The front-end, also known as the presentation layer, would handle the user interface and user experience for the Health Account’s Data Management System. It would consist of technologies like HTML, CSS and Javascript that can be rendered through a web browser on desktops and mobile devices.

The front-end tier in a single page application (SPA) typically follows Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture, which separates the concerns of the application into three distinct components \- the data (model), the user interface (view), and the logic that binds the two (controller).

* The Model represents the data and the business logic of the application. It can retrieve data from the server via an API or manage data entered by the user.  
* The View represents the user interface of the application. It is responsible for displaying the data to the user and collecting input from the user.  
* The Controller is the component that sits between the Model and the View. It is responsible for receiving user input, updating the Model based on that input, and updating the View to reflect any changes in the data.

In a SPA, the front-end tier communicates with the server via APIs to retrieve and update data. This allows the front-end to operate independently of the back-end, improving scalability and maintainability of the application.

Such separation of concerns would allow for more modular and maintainable code and makes it easier to update the user interface without impacting the rest of the application.

**![][image10]**

### API \- Application Programming Interface Layer/Tier 

The API acts as a standard channel for the application to interact with the Business Logic & Rules. API Generally encompasses the Business Logic layer too, which is responsible for implementing the functionality required to support the business process. 

The API Layer provides a reusable set of services that can be consumed by the front-end application. If required, the APIs can be used to exchange data with other external systems in an industry-standard manner. The API layer also provides help in decoupling the front-end and back-end layers of the application, allowing them to be developed and maintained independently. This means changes to one layer will not affect the other, allowing for more flexibility and scalability.

### Data Access Layer

The data layer refers to the part of the application that deals with storing, retrieving and manipulating data. It abstracts the underlying data storage mechanism and provides a consistent way for the rest of the application to interact with the data. With abstraction, it automatically provides portability, where it is easier to port the application to a different data storage mechanism.

In the 3-tier architecture, the front-end tier is typically separate from the other two tiers (business logic and data) to allow for flexibility in design and implementation and to make it easier to update, maintain and modify components without impacting the other parts of the application. The front-end, API, and data tiers can be scaled independently, making it easier to handle increased user traffic or changes in system requirements.

### Home Dashboard

The dashboard is the first screen a user sees after signing in, and we have designed it to answer the questions a Health Accounts analyst actually asks at the start of a working session. Every element on it is a link into the record it describes, so the dashboard works as a queue of things to do rather than a summary to read and leave.

The **Reporting Round** panel shows where the current cycle stands: which countries have submitted, which are still outstanding, and which are approaching or past their due date. It draws on the reporting schedule and focal point details held in the Setup module, and it is the panel the team will use most often between submissions. Beside it, **Publication Readiness** shows how many countries sit at Not publish and how many have moved to Ready to publish, which gives an immediate sense of how much of the round is finished. **Quality Findings** summarises the outcome of recent quality check runs by severity, with a link straight to the affected country and observation. **Data Completeness** presents coverage across countries and years as a heat map so that gaps stand out visually and can be turned into follow up. **Recent Activity** lists submissions received, changes made and the user's outstanding notifications.

Content on the dashboard is filtered by the signed in user's role and country scope, so a Regional Office colleague sees their own countries and an administrator sees the whole picture. The requirements also describe separate dashboards for administrators and regular users as a later addition. Our proposal delivers a common dashboard first, filtered by permission, and then adds the role specific layouts in the agreed phase, with the administrator view gaining operational content such as integration health, background job status and recent configuration changes.

*Home dashboard: reporting round, publication readiness, quality findings and data completeness.*

### Users and Role Management

This module gives administrators one place to control who can use the DMS and what they can do inside it. Sign in is handled entirely by WHO Single Sign On through Entra ID, so the application never stores or manages a password. Both WHO internal staff and external contributors are supported, the latter as guest accounts in Entra ID, and both follow the same sign in path. On the client side we recommend **MSAL** for the authentication flow, with the server validating tokens through standard **OpenID Connect** middleware.

An administrator grants access from the **Users** list by entering a colleague's WHO account or guest email address and choosing a role. The identity itself is established by Entra ID at first sign in, so the DMS record carries the authorization rather than the credential. The system provides the two roles the requirements define, Administrator and Regular user, and an administrator holds every capability a regular user holds in addition to the administrative ones, so there is no function that a regular user can reach and an administrator cannot.

Permissions are configuration rather than code. On the **Role Permissions** screen an administrator sets, for each module, the level that applies to regular users, choosing from the levels the requirements define: no access, view, view and export, edit selected countries, edit all, and full administrative control. Only the levels that carry meaning for a given module are offered, so "edit selected countries" is available on the Workbook but not on Users. Regular users keep view and export rights on the modules they cannot edit, which means the configuration can never produce a user who is unable to see the data they are responsible for. A **Capability Preview** panel beside the matrix shows in plain language what a regular user will and will not be able to do once the change is saved, which removes most of the guesswork from permission changes. Changes take effect immediately and are written to the audit log.

Access for a regular user can also be restricted to a defined list of countries, so that a Regional or Country Office colleague works only within their own countries. The restriction is applied in the API layer, which means it governs every module consistently, including the Workbook, reports, quality checks and every export, rather than being applied screen by screen where one path could be missed.

When someone leaves a post or changes responsibilities, their access is withdrawn using **Disable user** and can be restored later with **Enable user**, keeping all of their history and authorship intact. The system will not allow the last remaining enabled administrator to be disabled or moved to the Regular user role, so the platform cannot be left with nobody able to administer it. In line with the requirements, DMS users are never deleted. User records are referenced by observation authorship, version histories, rule and report ownership and audit entries, and removing a user would break the traceability those references provide. There is therefore no delete action anywhere in the module, and withdrawal of access is always achieved by disabling the account.

*Users list with inline role and status controls.*
