### Setup and Configuration

The Setup module is where the Health Accounts team defines the vocabulary the rest of the system uses. Each configurable component sits on its own tab within a consistent list and editor pattern, so the interaction a user learns on one component applies to all of them. Every tab is addressable by its own URL, which means a colleague can be sent straight to the right screen.

Configuration begins by importing the reference data already held in the warehouse, so the DMS starts aligned with xMart rather than from an empty state. Later changes made in the DMS are written back to xMart. The module manages **Countries** and their attributes, **Currencies**, **Classifications and Categories**, **Crosses**, **Observation Metadata Fields** and **Formulas**, with values created, edited and, where the requirements allow, disabled and enabled through the interface.

Several behaviours in this module are worth describing specifically. Columns in any component list can be reordered by dragging the column headers, and the chosen order is remembered for that user across sessions, which matters because different colleagues work with different attributes. Deleting a value is permitted only where that value has never been used in any record, as the requirements state, so before removing anything the system checks usage and, where the value is in use, reports where it is used instead of simply refusing. Administrators can define new attributes for existing components and edit component details, so the metadata model can be extended without a code change. Component values and their attributes can be exported to a spreadsheet and imported again, which makes bulk maintenance and offline review practical. For the spreadsheet handling in this module and elsewhere we recommend **ClosedXML** or **EPPlus** on the server and **SheetJS** in the browser, with **CsvHelper** for CSV work.

Country attributes can be flagged as available for grouping and filtering, which is what turns an attribute such as WHO region, World Bank income group or OECD membership into a selectable **Group of countries**. Because groups are defined once here, they appear everywhere a country selection is offered, including quality check scope, report filters and workbook selection, and they stay correct as membership changes.

The module also records the reporting schedule for each country, including due dates and focal point details, which is what drives the dashboard's reporting round view and the due date reminders described under Notifications. Each country and year carries a publishing status of **Not publish** or **Ready to publish**, which can be set on a single record or applied in bulk to a selection, so an entire round can be moved to publication readiness in one action.

**Crosses** deserve a note because they are easy to model incorrectly. A cross is not a separate kind of record. It is an observation that carries values in more than one classification dimension at the same time, which is exactly how the long format observation table in xMart represents it. Modelling crosses this way keeps the Workbook, the Crosses tab and the warehouse structure consistent with one another. Predefined crosses are configured centrally, and users can define additional custom crosses for their own analysis. Metadata files already held in xMart are reachable from the DMS in the context of the observation or country they relate to, so supporting documentation does not require leaving the application.

*Setup module showing the component tabs and a component list.*

### 

### Workbook Management

The Workbook is the main working module of the DMS and the screen on which the Health Accounts team will spend most of its time. The requirements describe it clearly: a format similar to Excel, in which the values available for a country and year can be viewed and edited, formulas inserted, and copy, paste and undo used as they would be in a spreadsheet, with the metadata behind each observation reachable from the same place.

A workbook is a two dimensional view of a three dimensional dataset, formed by fixing one axis and displaying the other two. A **Country Workbook** shows one country against many variables and many years. A **Variable Workbook** shows one variable across many countries and many years. A **Year Workbook** shows one year across many countries and many variables. The user chooses the type and the scope, and the selection is reflected in the address of the page so that a particular view can be bookmarked, returned to or shared with a colleague.

Years run across the top and variables down the side, with a scale and currency selector above the grid so that figures can be read in the units the analyst is thinking in. Reported values and calculated indicators are visually distinct: as the requirements specify, formula cells are shown in a different colour and in italic, so a calculated figure is never mistaken for one a country reported. The year header row, the variable label column and the corner cell are all **frozen**, which means the context of a cell stays visible however far the user scrolls. Scrolling itself is continuous and virtualized rather than paged, because paging a data entry surface breaks range selection and makes copying a block of years across impossible.

Editing happens in place and follows spreadsheet conventions, so typing replaces, Enter and Tab commit and move on, and Escape abandons the edit. Formulas can be typed directly into a cell and are evaluated straight away, with every dependent indicator recalculating as soon as an input changes, so the effect of a correction is visible immediately rather than after a refresh. Copying and pasting works within a workbook and across workbooks, and the paste action distinguishes between pasting **Values**, **Formulas** and **Metadata**, because in Health Accounts work those are three different intentions. A multi level **Undo** and **Redo** stack covers edits, pastes, fills and bulk operations, so a mistaken paste over a block of data is recoverable.

Filtering is available on any displayed element. Rather than a permanent row of dropdown boxes, active filters appear as removable chips above the grid with an **Add filter** control beside them, so the current filter set can be read at a glance and any one filter reopened or removed in a single action. The filter state travels in the page address, which makes a filtered view shareable.

Metadata is reached from the grid itself. Cells that carry metadata are marked, and opening one opens a panel **beside** the grid rather than over it. The grid stays loaded and the cell selection is preserved, so reading a comment or checking a source does not cost the analyst their place in the data. This is a deliberate departure from the legacy tool, where metadata lived on a separate sheet. Editing metadata is subject to the same permissions, versioning and write back as editing a value. Users can also choose which metadata fields are displayed and in what order, and that preference is remembered.

The module provides the estimation tools the requirements ask for. **Fill gaps** completes missing points between two existing values in a series, and **Extrapolate** extends a series backwards or forwards, with the method chosen by the user. Observations produced this way are marked with the appropriate estimation method and data type so their origin stays visible in exports and reports afterwards. Alongside these, the workbook supports the calculation of standard indicators for all countries, simple statistical values such as average, minimum and maximum across a selected group of countries, and country specific formulas for estimation, which are saved for reuse.

Because the requirements are explicit that only one user may edit the same observations at a time, the workbook applies a lock when editing begins. Other users keep read only access and are shown who holds the lock and since when, rather than simply being refused. Locks are released on save, or after a configurable interval once a session ends, and an administrator can release a lock that has been left open. Workbook data can be exported to Excel. Quality check rules can also be run directly from the workbook against the data in view, with failing cells highlighted where they sit.

*Workbook with frozen headers, filter chips, calculated rows shown distinctly, and the metadata panel open beside the grid.*

### Formula Management and Calculation Engine

The calculation engine is the technical heart of the DMS. We treat the engine as a distinct piece of engineering rather than a feature of the Workbook, and we build it rather than adapt a spreadsheet engine, for four reasons that come directly from the requirements.

First, Health Accounts formulas refer to variables, not to cells. An expression such as CHE \= HF.1 \+ HF.2 \+ HF.3 \+ HF.4 \+ HF.nec names classification categories that are resolved for the current country and year. Second, formulas refer to other formulas. CHE%GDP depends on CHE, which in turn depends on the HF categories, so evaluation needs a dependency graph resolved in the right order with cycles detected, not text substitution. Third, every formula carries its own condition for handling missing values. The indicator table in the requirements attaches a condition to each one: some require all components to be present, others at least one. When a condition is not met the result must be blank and not zero, because a zero asserts that expenditure was nil while a blank says it is unknown, and that difference is visible in every published figure. Fourth, a predefined formula must be adjustable for one country without changing it for any other, so the engine resolves the applicable definition per country at the point of evaluation.

The engine is built as a tokenizer, a parser producing a syntax tree, a dependency graph over the referenced variables, and an evaluator that walks that graph in dependency order. Cycles are caught when a formula is saved rather than when it is run, so an invalid formula cannot be committed in the first place. Variable codes in this domain contain full stops, percent signs, currency symbols and hyphens, as in CHE%GDP\_SHA2011 and GGHE-D\_pc\_US\$\_SHA2011, so references are resolved against the known set of variables rather than by guessing where a token ends, which is a common and quiet source of error. For the grammar we recommend **ANTLR** where a formally specified grammar is preferred, or a hand written recursive descent parser where a small and fully owned implementation is more appropriate. We would avoid general purpose expression libraries for the core engine, since none of them carry per country overrides or the null handling conditions this domain requires.

Administrators manage the predefined indicators on the **Formulas** tab in Setup, each with its expression, its condition for missing values, its unit of measure and its folder grouping. A predefined formula can be edited, and a **Country Override** can be created that applies to one country alone. Regular users can write their own formulas and save them for reuse, and these pass through exactly the same parsing, validation and cycle checking.

Because the engine holds an explicit dependency graph, the application can show a user why a figure is what it is. A **Formula Inspector** panel presents the expression, the inputs it resolved to, the condition that was applied, and the chain of other indicators that will change if an input changes. For a system whose outputs are published internationally, being able to explain a number is as important as calculating it.

*Formula management with the predefined indicator formulas and their conditions.*

### Quality Checks

The Quality Checks module is how the team validates itself that a dataset is fit to publish. It holds a library of rules, the means to run them over a chosen scope, and a report of what they found.

Rules are grouped by type, with a separate group for a user's own customized rules. Rules created by the development team during implementation, rules created by administrators and rules created by individual users are visually distinct from one another, as the requirements ask, so the standing of a rule is clear from the list rather than having to be looked up.

We will implement the predefined rule categories the requirements describe, with the final list confirmed by the technical unit at project start and the examples in the requirements as the starting point. These cover year on year growth in absolute and relative terms, growth between two versions of the data, observations that are new, that have disappeared or that are missing compared with previous reporting, inconsistency between categories where components should reconcile to their total, inconsistency between tables, atypical entries raised either as an error or as a warning, and outliers assessed across groups of countries.

The thresholds that decide whether a rule passes, fails or raises a warning are set by administrators on a **Thresholds** screen rather than fixed in code, so the team can tune sensitivity as the data and their expectations change, without waiting for a release. Rules apply to every country by default, and an administrator can exclude specific countries where a rule is not meaningful for them, then **Reset exclusions** to make the rule universal again. Exclusions are shown on the rule itself, so an excluded country is never quietly left unchecked.

A rule is run against a single country or against a group of countries chosen by attribute, using the same groups configured in Setup. The full year end run across all countries executes as a background job with visible progress, restart and retry, so a long run can be watched and recovered rather than simply waited on. Rules can also be triggered from a workbook against the data currently in view, with failing cells highlighted in place, which closes the gap between finding a problem and fixing it: the analyst does not have to carry a finding from a report back into the data by hand.

Each run produces a report presenting findings by rule, by country and by severity, with charts alongside the tabular detail and a download in Excel or CSV. Every finding links directly to the observation that produced it. Rule configurations can be exported and imported, which supports review outside the system and moving a configuration between environments.

*Quality check rule library, with rule origin visually distinguished.*

### Reports and Analytics

The Reports module produces the outputs the team needs for internal review, quality assurance and preparing the year's publication.

Administrators define reports in an interactive builder. Available fields, including countries and their attributes, years, classifications and categories, variables and indicators, and metadata fields, are dragged into **Rows**, **Columns**, **Filters** and **Values** areas to form a multi dimensional view. The Values area takes the aggregations of the observation measure, and subtotals can be switched on at any grouping level. A live preview updates as the definition changes, so a report is designed against real output rather than against an abstract specification. Saved reports become available to everyone. In line with the requirements the builder is an administrator function: regular users open predefined reports, apply filters and export the results.

A regular user can also create customized reports that are visible only to themselves, and any user can copy an existing report as the basis for a new one, which is usually the quickest route to a variant of an established output. Users arrange reports into their own list, mark **Favourites** and set the order, so a working set is always at hand.

The module includes data tracking reports covering what has been received, what has changed and what is still outstanding across the reporting round, which supports the follow up process configured in Setup.

Although the interface itself is in English, reports can be generated with variable labels in any of the six official WHO languages: English, French, Spanish, Arabic, Chinese and Russian. Column headings, classification and indicator labels, totals and unit strings all appear in the chosen language, on screen and in the exported file. Field values that are proper names, such as country and currency names, report titles and free text metadata, stay as recorded, which is the carve out the requirement itself makes. We use **i18next** for the language resources, kept outside the code so that a label correction or an additional language is a configuration change.

Reports export to Excel. Where the scope of a report makes generation slow, it runs as a background job so the user can carry on working, and an in app notification arrives on completion with a link to the file, or on failure with the reason. Job progress and history are visible in the module.

Unit handling in this module is treated as a matter of correctness rather than formatting. Health Accounts values are expressed in national currency units, in US dollars or as percentages, so conversion is applied to each observation before aggregation, and the unit label carries the country's own currency rather than a generic one. Where the contributions to a total arrived in more than one currency, the report produces no figure at all, because adding pesos to yen is meaningless and an anonymous unit label would let exactly that mistake through looking perfectly correct.

*Report builder with the field areas and live preview.*

### 

### Data and Metadata Versioning

Versioning is built on the data versioning available in xMart, as the requirements direct, rather than on a parallel history kept in the DMS. Every committed change to an observation, a dataset or a metadata field produces a version carrying its author and the time it was made.

Users with the appropriate rights can view up to ten previous versions of an observation or variable and compare them, with differences in value and in metadata shown side by side so that what changed, when and by whom is legible at a glance. From the same screen a previous version can be selected and restored as the current value. Administrators can additionally restore a full dataset as at a specific date, which is the recovery path when a bulk operation has produced an unintended result.

Restoration is itself recorded as a version, so history is never rewritten. Restoring an earlier value adds a new entry describing that restoration rather than removing the entries in between, which keeps the record complete for audit purposes. Version comparison also feeds the quality check category concerned with growth between two versions of the data, so versioning serves validation as well as recovery.

*Version history for a single observation, with restore.*

### Notifications

The Notifications module provides the event driven, in application notifications the requirements describe.

Notifications are raised on defined events: a country's submission arriving, a reporting due date approaching or passing, a background report or quality check finishing or failing, a dataset moving to **Ready to publish**, a version being restored, or a configuration or permission change being applied. A predefined set is delivered with the system, based on the list the technical unit provides at project start.

Administrators create and edit notifications, setting the event that triggers each one and the countries or groups of countries it applies to for each user. Because the groups are the same ones configured in Setup, a subscription such as "all countries in the African Region" is expressed once and stays correct as the membership of that group changes. Users control what reaches them through **Notification Preferences**, choosing the countries and variables they care about, so that colleagues receive what is relevant to their responsibilities rather than every event in the system.

Notifications are delivered in the application and highlighted on the dashboard, with an unread count in the header. Where a notification refers to something the user can open, such as a completed report or a quality check result, it carries a working link to it. The reporting due dates configured in Setup raise reminders as dates approach and pass, which is what turns the follow up configuration into an active process rather than a reference table someone has to remember to consult.

*Notifications module: event catalogue and subscriptions.*

### Integration with WHO xMart

Integration with xMart is not a feature at the edge of this system. It is the mechanism by which the system holds its data, and the requirements define the exchange in both directions.

Whenever the DMS needs to display or process Health Accounts information it retrieves that information from xMart through the secured xMart API. This covers observations for the Workbook, the configuration behind the Setup module, the data underlying reports and quality checks, and version information. Retrieval is designed to ask only for what the screen needs, filtered by country, year range and the variables in scope, so that opening a workbook fetches one bounded slice rather than a country's entire history.

Changes made in the DMS are returned to xMart so that the warehouse stays authoritative. This covers observation values and metadata edited in the Workbook, and changes made in Setup to countries, currencies, classifications, categories, crosses, metadata fields and formulas. Each write back carries the identity of the user who made the change, as the requirements specify, and again keeps values as values and formulas as formulas.

The requirements leave the trigger for write back to be agreed at the start of the project, offering a save action or simply leaving a screen as the possibilities. Our recommendation is an explicit **Save**, with a clearly marked unsaved changes state on the screen. It gives the analyst a defined point at which work is committed, it makes a concurrent editing conflict detectable at a known moment, and it produces a version history whose entries correspond to deliberate decisions rather than to incidental navigation. From the user's point of view a save either succeeds completely or reports a failure naming the observations affected, and a failed transmission is queued for retry with the outcome visible to the user and to administrators.

Alongside consuming the xMart API, the DMS exposes a data retrieval API that xMart calls to extract DMS data. We will implement this to the specification in the API requirements: HTTP GET requests, CSV as the default output with JSON available as well, filtering on country code and on a single year or year range, the DMS internal identifier returned on every row, server side paging designed around the reference page size of one hundred thousand records, a UTC LastModified value that can be filtered by range and that reflects inserts, updates and deletes alike, retrieval of soft deleted records through an IsDeleted filter, the ability to return all data unfiltered, streamed responses for large extractions, OAuth 2.0 authentication and HTTPS only transport.

Two of those items are treated as first class design requirements rather than reporting conveniences. Every path in the application that modifies data updates the LastModified value, and deletion is implemented as a change of state rather than a physical removal, so a record that disappears from the DMS can still be identified as deleted by a caller that asks for it.

For administrators the module also provides operational visibility. **Sync Status** shows, per source and per direction, when data was last retrieved, when changes were last written back, what is pending and what has failed. An **API Call Log** records requests to and from xMart with their outcome, duration and payload size, so an integration problem can be diagnosed from evidence rather than reconstructed. Failed exchanges are queued, retried according to policy and escalated by notification when retries are exhausted. Background jobs covering quality check runs, report generation and bulk exports are monitored from the same place.

Finally, the requirements ask that functionality be implemented within the xMart platform itself wherever doing so saves effort and cost, and state that WHO will give credit to solutions that use xMart technology even partially. We have taken this into account in shaping the architecture. We propose to use xMart for the storage and data model of observations, metadata and configuration, rather than replicating that structure in the DMS; for native data versioning, on which the version history and restore functions are built; for format validation and transformation on ingestion, which the process map already places in xMart; for views and derived structures where a view is cheaper and faster than an equivalent query assembled in the application; for holding the legacy formulas imported from the old system as metadata; and for onboarding and updating model definitions through the xMart Model Uploader, a capability our team has already used in production on the WHO Emergency Public Dashboard. The interactive and rule driven functionality, meaning the Workbook, the calculation engine, the quality check engine, the report builder, user and permission management, notifications, job orchestration and the retrieval API, is implemented in the DMS database, where that kind of logic belongs. Our existing familiarity with the xMart OData API and the Model Uploader means this assessment can be confirmed and refined quickly during discovery rather than being settled after development has started.

*xMart integration: synchronisation status and the API call log.*

### Legacy Data and Formula Migration

The legacy DMS holds the Health Accounts history the new system needs to be able to consult, together with approximately seventy thousand formulas in its Microsoft SQL Server database. Argusoft will manage the migration of this content into the agreed xMart and DMS target structures as a controlled and reconciled process rather than a single transfer.

We begin by profiling the legacy schema, its data quality and its formula syntax, and producing a source to target mapping agreed with WHO. Extraction takes the latest version of each record and each formula, in line with the requirement that only the latest version is migrated. Transformation maps legacy identifiers onto the classification and category codes in use in the new system. Loading places the data in xMart, with the legacy formulas stored as plain text metadata fields so that each is available for inquiry from the new DMS against the observations it relates to.

The formulas are then translated into working formulas in the new DMS. The calculation engine described earlier is what makes this systematic rather than manual: because it parses an expression into a syntax tree instead of treating it as text, converting a legacy formula is a matter of re-expressing a parsed structure in the new syntax. The conversion is carried out together with the WHO Health Accounts team, whose knowledge of the legacy formula population is what allows individual cases to be settled authoritatively, and each converted formula is validated by comparing its computed result against the legacy result for the same country and year.

Reconciliation produces record counts, control totals and an exception report naming any formula that needs individual attention and why, so that anything outstanding is a known and jointly managed list rather than a silent gap. The migration is run at least twice in a non production environment before the production run, so that the reconciliation report rather than the cutover is where problems come to light, and a documented rollback position is established before the production run begins. WHO signs off against the reconciliation evidence before cutover.

### Additional Features

Report output is available with variable labels in the six official WHO languages, as described under Reports and Analytics. Language resources are held outside the application code using **i18next**, so adding a language or correcting a label does not require a code change. Labels are translated while codes, unit keys and stored filter values stay canonical, which matters because a translated unit key would stop the currency checks in the reporting engine comparing like with like.

The application will be developed to meet the applicable WHO accessibility requirements, covering keyboard navigation, focus order, form labelling, colour contrast and compatibility with assistive technology. We treat this as a design constraint from the first wireframe rather than as remediation at the end. The workbook reinforces its use of colour with typography so that the distinction between reported and calculated cells does not depend on colour alone.

The application supports the browsers and viewport sizes agreed with WHO, verified by cross browser testing with **Playwright**. Layouts are responsive across desktop and laptop sizes. The Workbook, being a dense data entry surface, is designed for desktop use, which reflects how the team actually works.

Every data change, configuration change, permission change, quality check run, report generation and integration event is written to an audit trail carrying the user's identity, a timestamp and a description of the action. Administrators reach it through a searchable and filterable **Audit Log** view. Logs are structured using **Serilog** and can be shipped to a central platform such as the **ELK stack** or Azure Monitor for retention and analysis.

### Security Features

Security is described in detail under *Approach* earlier in this proposal, and the points below cover how it appears in the design of the solution itself.

Authentication is delegated entirely to WHO Entra ID, so the application holds no passwords and inherits WHO's own account policies, including multi factor authentication. Authorization is enforced in the API layer, covering role permissions and country restrictions together, which means it cannot be bypassed by manipulating the client. All traffic runs over HTTPS, and the data retrieval API that xMart calls is protected with OAuth 2.0.

Data is encrypted in transit and at rest using WHO approved Azure services and configurations, with keys held in **Azure Key Vault** and separated from the application. Uploaded files are validated for type and size and scanned for malware using the security scan API WHO provides, and a file that fails either check is rejected before it reaches storage.

The application is built following OWASP secure coding practices, with input validation, output encoding, parameterised queries and secure session handling applied throughout, and least privilege applied to every service account. Our development process includes static application security testing, software composition analysis and dependency scanning, secret scanning, and dynamic application security testing before release.

## Proposed Work Plan {#proposed-work-plan}

Our work plan is aligned with the implementation approach, milestones, and deliverables defined in the Terms of Reference. It follows a hybrid delivery model that combines structured planning with iterative Agile development, enabling continuous stakeholder engagement, phased delivery, and early validation throughout the project lifecycle. Each phase concludes with defined review and approval checkpoints to ensure quality, transparency, and controlled progression before moving to the next stage.

In parallel with the phase-wise activities described below, Argusoft will maintain key project management artefacts including the Project Management Plan, Sprint Backlog, Risk & Issue Register, Change Log, Quality Assurance Plan, and Project Status Reports. These artefacts will be reviewed and updated throughout the engagement to support effective project governance, communication, and progress monitoring.

### Phase 1: Project Initiation & Requirements Gathering

Following contract signing, Argusoft will conduct a project kick-off meeting with the WHO Health Accounts team to establish project governance, communication mechanisms, timelines, and reporting arrangements. Detailed requirement gathering workshops will be conducted to validate functional and non-functional requirements, study the existing DMS, understand business processes for data import, analysis, verification, and publication, review xMart capabilities, API specifications, and legacy data structures, and confirm integration and migration requirements. The findings will form the foundation for solution design and implementation.

**Deliverables**

* Project Management Plan  
* Technical Requirement Study  
* Validated Functional & Technical Requirements  
* Updated Implementation Work Plan

### Phase 2: Solution Design & Prototype Development

Based on the validated requirements, Argusoft will prepare the technical and graphical design of the solution, including the overall architecture, DMS data model, integration design, security design, wireframes, UI/UX prototypes, deployment architecture and Azure cloud resource-sizing requirements. The proposed design will be presented to WHO for review and approval before development activities commence. Argusoft will establish and operate the Development environment using vendor-provided infrastructure. WHO will provide the Azure subscription, licenses and required access. Argusoft will provision, configure, deploy and maintain the UAT and Production environments within WHO’s Azure subscription using approved IaC and DevOps practices.

**Deliverables**

* System Design Document  
* Wireframes / UI-UX Prototypes  
* Hardware Requirement Proposal  
* Approved Technical & Graphical Design


### Phase 3: System Development, Integration & Pilot Implementation

Development will be delivered through two-to-three-week Agile sprints, implementing the Pilot functionality first and then the remaining agreed requirements. The Pilot will include a general dashboard; advanced role-specific dashboards for administrators and regular users may be delivered under Priority 3\. This phase includes the DMS application and APIs, bidirectional xMart integration, quality assurance, and UAT milestone deployments for WHO working-group functional acceptance. Argusoft will also perform the one-time migration of legacy Health Accounts data and approximately 70,000 legacy formulas from the old DMS, including loading formula metadata into xMart and conversion to the new DMS formula syntax as required by UC060. Existing external-source pipelines into xMart are already in place and are outside DMS development scope.

**Deliverables**

* Pilot DMS Functionalities  
* Remaining Functional Modules  
* Interim Demonstrations  
* UAT Deployments  
* Integrated and Tested System Components

### Phase 4: System Testing & User Acceptance

Comprehensive testing will be conducted to verify that all system modules comply with the agreed functional requirements and acceptance criteria. This phase includes system testing, integration testing, performance testing, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), issue resolution, and final validation in collaboration with the WHO Health Accounts team before production deployment.

**Deliverables**

* Quality Assurance & Testing Reports  
* User Acceptance Testing (UAT) Completion  
* Final Demonstration  
* Production Readiness Approval

### 

### Phase 5: Production Deployment, Training & Knowledge Transfer

Following successful UAT, the Health Accounts Data Management System will be deployed to the WHO Production environment. Administrator and user training will be conducted, followed by handover of all project artefacts, including technical documentation, database documentation, source code, system architecture documentation, user and administrator guides, and third-party licence keys (where applicable).

**Deliverables**

* Deployment of DMS on Production Server  
* Training of Users and Administrators  
* Training Report  
* Database Technical Documentation  
* Source Code & Technical Documentation  
* System Architecture Documentation  
* User & Administrator Guides  
* Third-Party Licence Keys (if applicable)


### Phase 6: Warranty, Cloud Infrastructure Support & Project Closure

Cloud infrastructure support and monitoring for UAT and Production will begin when the WHO-hosted environments are established and continue through implementation and the three-month warranty, which is included within the overall ten-month project period. Following Production deployment, Argusoft will provide 8x5 warranty support covering issue resolution, defect correction, Azure infrastructure assistance, monitoring, SSL-certificate monitoring, troubleshooting and Monthly Support & Maintenance Reports. Post-warranty support will be treated as a separate assignment.

**Deliverables**

* Warranty Services (3 Months)  
* Monthly Support & Maintenance Reports  
* Project Completion Report

## Quality Assurance Methodologies and Processes {#quality-assurance-methodologies-and-processes}

Argusoft will apply a quality-first, risk-based assurance approach to ensure that the Health Accounts Data Management System (DMS) satisfies WHO’s functional, technical, integration, security, accessibility, migration and performance requirements. Quality assurance will be embedded throughout requirements validation, architecture and design, iterative development, integration, deployment and warranty support. Reviews, sprint demonstrations and formal validation checkpoints will provide progressive evidence that each contractual deliverable meets its approved acceptance criteria.

### Test Strategy, Environments and Responsibilities

Argusoft will prepare a Master Test Plan covering test scope, approach, responsibilities, environments, test data, traceability, entry and exit criteria, defect management, reporting and acceptance evidence. Development-level, component and integration testing will be performed in the vendor-provided Development environment. Formal system verification and UAT will be conducted in the WHO-provided UAT environment using WHO-provided representative test data and xMart UAT access. As WHO has confirmed that no existing test cases or API regression suite are available, Argusoft will create the functional, integration, migration, formula-validation, security, performance and regression test assets required for the project.

### Requirements Traceability and Acceptance

Argusoft will maintain a Requirements Traceability Matrix mapping each ToR objective and high-level requirement to the applicable use case, design component, sprint, test scenario and test case, UAT result, defect status and final acceptance status. This traceability will demonstrate coverage of all required use cases and support milestone-level acceptance.

The WHO working group will provide milestone and final acceptance based on applicable functional and operational test results. For each acceptance decision, Argusoft will submit the current traceability matrix, executed test evidence, defect status, migration and formula reconciliation results, security findings and remediation status, performance results, and a release-readiness or Test Completion Report.

### Entry and Exit Criteria

Each test cycle will have documented entry and exit criteria. Entry criteria will include approved requirements and acceptance criteria, an available and stable test environment, a deployed test build, available interfaces, representative test data and completed developer testing. Exit criteria will include completion of planned tests, agreed requirements coverage, successful regression testing, resolution of all Critical and High-severity defects, documented disposition and WHO acceptance of any remaining lower-severity defects, and approval of the applicable Test Completion Report.

### Defect Severity and Release Controls

Defects will be recorded, triaged, prioritized, assigned, corrected, re-tested and closed through a controlled issue-management workflow:

* Critical – system unavailability, security exposure, data corruption or failure of a critical process without a viable workaround; must be resolved before release.  
* High – failure of a major function or business process without an acceptable workaround; must be resolved before release.  
* Medium – impaired functionality for which a reasonable workaround exists; must be resolved or formally accepted for deferred correction.  
* Low – minor usability, presentation or documentation issue; tracked and prioritized through the agreed backlog.

The final severity definitions, service expectations and approval authority will be confirmed during inception. No Production release will proceed with unresolved Critical or High-severity defects.

### Functional, Workbook, Formula and Quality-Check Testing

Functional testing will verify all approved business processes and use cases, including users and roles, country-level access, configuration, classifications and crosses, metadata, workbooks, formulas, reports, versions, notifications, audit trails and administration. Workbook testing will include locking and concurrent read-only access, copy/paste, undo, filtering, import/export, formula/value handling, recalculation, version comparison and restoration.

Formula testing will verify syntax conversion, expected calculation results, rounding and precision, null and zero behaviour, divide-by-zero and invalid-reference handling, country/year/classification references, recalculation triggers, auditability and exception reporting. Quality Check module testing will cover predefined and customized rules, administrator and regular-user permissions, country/group applicability and exclusions, Passed/Failed/Error/Warning outcomes, manual workbook-triggered execution, Excel export and re-import of rule configuration, report generation and storage, and full year-end execution for approximately 196 countries. Retry, restart, progress visibility, job status and result consistency will also be verified against WHO-approved rules and representative expected results.

### DMS–xMart Integration and API Testing

Argusoft will validate the bidirectional DMS–xMart interfaces, including API contracts, OAuth 2.0 authentication, HTTPS, CSV and optional JSON output, business-key and date-range filtering, internal identifiers, paging designed for the Annex 3 reference page size of 100,000 records, streaming, complete and incremental retrieval, range-filterable UTC LastModified values, inclusion or exclusion of soft-deleted records, update processing, error responses, retry behaviour and end-to-end data reconciliation. Existing external-source pipelines into xMart are outside the DMS development scope and will not be represented as direct DMS integrations.

### Legacy Data, Metadata and Formula Migration Testing

Migration assurance will validate source-to-target mappings, record counts, mandatory fields, data types, referential integrity, duplicate handling, metadata associations, formula extraction and conversion, reconciliation totals, exception handling and audit evidence. Testing will cover the legacy data and approximately 70,000 formulas stored in the old DMS SQL Server, subject to the detailed migration and conversion rules agreed during discovery. Validation will use full-population checks where practical and WHO-approved sampling for fields or calculations requiring business review. A failed-conversion and reconciliation exception report will support correction and formal sign-off.

### Performance, Reliability and Recovery Testing

During discovery, Argusoft and WHO will agree representative performance scenarios and measurable thresholds for interactive workbook operations, API calls, report generation, imports and exports, migration processing and year-end quality-check execution. Tests will cover workloads ranging from small selections to the stated 25-million-row maximum using server-side paging, streaming, asynchronous or background processing, or bulk extraction as appropriate; the design will not assume that all records are loaded interactively into a browser.

Performance and reliability testing will also cover approximately 20 concurrent internal users, the confirmed xMart batch capability, queue processing, progress visibility, restart and retry behaviour, failed-job recovery, notifications and sustained stability. Backup, restoration and recovery procedures will be tested against WHO-agreed recovery objectives before Production readiness.

### Security, Accessibility and Compatibility Testing

Security assurance will be supported by Argusoft’s in-house cybersecurity team, including professionals holding certifications such as HTB CPTS, CompTIA Security+ and eJPT. Activities will include threat modelling, peer review, static application security testing, software-composition analysis, dependency and secret scanning, dynamic application security testing, authentication and authorization testing, API security testing, audit-log verification, input validation, country- and role-based access testing, and remediation verification before Production release. File-upload controls and malware scanning will be validated using the WHO-provided security scan API.

Accessibility testing will validate the applicable WHO accessibility requirements, keyboard navigation, focus order, labels, contrast and assistive-technology compatibility. Cross-browser and responsive testing will verify the supported user experience across the agreed browsers and viewport sizes.

### Regression, UAT, Deployment and Warranty Verification

A maintainable regression suite will be established because no existing suite is available. Automated regression testing will be applied where cost-effective and sustainable, supplemented by manual testing for complex workflows and visual or exploratory scenarios. Argusoft will support WHO during UAT, triage and classify defects and agreed observations, implement in-scope corrections and minor modifications, and re-test resolved items.

Before Production deployment, Argusoft will complete the agreed regression, security, migration-reconciliation, performance, backup/restore and release-readiness checks. During warranty, the team will monitor solution quality, reproduce and resolve reported defects, verify corrections and maintain traceability to the affected requirement and release.

### Quality Assurance Deliverables

The QA workstream will produce and maintain the following evidence:

* Master Test Plan and testing strategy.  
* Requirements Traceability Matrix.  
* Test scenarios, cases, scripts and representative test datasets.  
* API contract, integration and DMS–xMart reconciliation report.  
* Legacy data, metadata and formula migration reconciliation report.  
* Performance, reliability and recovery test report.  
* Accessibility and compatibility test report.  
* Security testing and remediation report.  
* UAT support, defect-closure and release-readiness report.  
* Test Completion Report for each contractual milestone.  
* Final consolidated testing and acceptance report.

This evidence-based assurance approach will provide WHO with transparent, measurable proof that the delivered DMS is functionally complete, secure, reliable, accessible, correctly integrated with xMart, accurately migrated and ready for sustainable operation by the WHO Health Accounts programme.

## Capacity Building and Knowledge Transfer {#capacity-building-and-knowledge-transfer}

### Capacity-Building Objective

Argusoft’s capacity-building approach will progressively transfer business, administrative, operational and technical knowledge to WHO so that designated personnel can confidently use, administer, operate, support and further develop the DMS. Knowledge transfer will be treated as a continuous project workstream and will culminate in a verified handover, rather than being limited to a single end-of-project activity.

### Continuous Knowledge Transfer

Knowledge transfer will be embedded throughout inception, design, development, migration, testing and deployment through requirements workshops, architecture and design walkthroughs, sprint demonstrations, configuration and workflow-validation sessions, migration-mapping and reconciliation reviews, formula-conversion walkthroughs, DMS–xMart API walkthroughs, UAT defect-triage participation, and deployment and operational-readiness reviews. Key decisions, procedures and lessons learned will be documented so that project knowledge is retained by WHO.

### Training-Needs Assessment and Plan

During inception, Argusoft will work with WHO to confirm participant roles, existing knowledge, priority workflows and administrator responsibilities. Based on this assessment, Argusoft will prepare a role-based training plan, agenda, practical exercises and representative scenarios using the approved WHO UAT environment and WHO-provided test data.

### Remote Training for WHO Experts

Argusoft will deliver one instructor-led remote training session in English for up to 20 WHO-designated experts. The agenda will include distinct segments for key/business users, administrators, and technical or operational personnel.

* Key and business users: navigation, workbooks, formulas, metadata, reports, Quality Checks, version history, notifications and common business workflows.  
* Administrators: users, roles, country-based access, system configuration, rule management, operational monitoring, audit logs and troubleshooting.  
* Technical and operational personnel: solution architecture, deployment, configuration, DMS–xMart interfaces, database, monitoring, backup and restoration, security operations and release procedures.

### Train-the-Trainer and Reusable Materials

The approach will follow a train-the-trainer model, enabling WHO-designated experts to support subsequent onboarding and internal knowledge dissemination. Materials will be supplied in editable and reusable formats where applicable and will include the training plan and agenda, presentation materials, role-based exercises, quick-reference guides, User Guide, Administrator Guide, frequently asked questions and troubleshooting guidance. A session recording will be provided subject to WHO approval and applicable policies.

### Technical and Operational Documentation

The handover documentation will include the Solution Architecture Document and diagrams; database schema, data types, table structures and data dictionary; API and xMart integration documentation; source-code and component documentation; configuration and environment guide; build, deployment, rollback, CI/CD and Infrastructure-as-Code procedures; monitoring, logging and alert-management runbook; backup, restoration and recovery procedures; security and access-control guide; migration mappings, formula-conversion rules and reconciliation records; Quality Check and formula-configuration guidance; known-issues and troubleshooting runbook; third-party component, dependency and licence inventory; and relevant testing, security-remediation and completion reports.

### Source Code and System Handover

Argusoft will hand over the complete project-specific application source code, database scripts, build and deployment assets, Infrastructure-as-Code, configuration templates, API specifications, technical documentation, testing artefacts and applicable third-party licence information through the repository and handover mechanism agreed with WHO. The package will include the instructions required to build, deploy, configure, operate, maintain and further enhance the solution. WHO will own the project-specific deliverables, subject to the licence terms applicable to third-party and open-source components.

### Training and Handover Acceptance

Training effectiveness will be assessed through attendance, completion of guided practical exercises, participant questions, a concise knowledge check and participant feedback. Material knowledge gaps will be addressed through updated guidance, written clarifications or handover materials. The Training Report will document attendance, topics covered, materials delivered, feedback, outstanding questions and follow-up actions.

Before final acceptance, Argusoft will conduct a structured handover walkthrough and jointly verify with the WHO working group that the source repository, documentation, deployment instructions, database specifications, guides, training materials, licence information and required project artefacts are complete and accessible. Any identified gaps will be resolved before submission of the Project Completion Report.

### Capacity-Building Deliverables

* Training Needs Assessment and Training Plan  
* Training agenda, presentation materials and practical exercises  
* User Guide and Administrator Guide  
* Quick-reference, FAQ and troubleshooting materials  
* Training attendance, feedback and knowledge-check records  
* Training Report  
* Technical and Operational Documentation Package  
* Source Code and Technical Artefact Handover Package  
* Third-Party Components and Licence Inventory  
* Handover Checklist and Acceptance Record  
* Project Completion Report

## Support, Maintenance & Warranty Services {#support,-maintenance-&-warranty-services}

Argusoft will provide application warranty and cloud-infrastructure support from Production deployment through completion of the three-month warranty period within the overall ten-month project. The warranty will cover all DMS modules and will include correction of defects, errors, functional gaps and operational issues, together with agreed feature enhancements, customizations and additional reports falling within the contractual scope. In accordance with WHO’s clarification, each individual modification that can be completed within 10 working days by one resource will be treated as in scope. Requests requiring more than 10 person-days will be jointly assessed by WHO and Argusoft and handled separately, as applicable. Up to 20% scope adjustment during development and warranty will be included in the proposed cost and planned and prioritized by the WHO working group.

Support beyond the warranty is outside the present assignment and may be provided through a separate assignment. Where requested in the Financial Proposal, Argusoft may provide indicative post-warranty support rates or options for WHO’s evaluation; any such services will be activated only through a separate contractual arrangement.

### Support Coverage and Responsibility Boundaries

Application support will cover DMS defects, failed jobs, workbook and formula issues, Quality Checks, reports, notifications, configuration and application logs. Integration support will cover diagnosis of bidirectional DMS–xMart interface failures, API errors and reconciliation issues, together with coordination with the WHO xMart team. Infrastructure support will cover the WHO-hosted UAT and Production Azure environments, including approved configuration, monitoring, certificates, deployment pipelines, Infrastructure-as-Code-controlled changes and troubleshooting. Security support will cover vulnerability triage, dependency and platform patching, security-event investigation, remediation and verification.

Changes to the xMart platform, WHO tenant and subscription administration, and existing external-source pipelines into xMart will remain with the appropriate WHO teams. Argusoft will nevertheless coordinate actively with WHO and Microsoft, where required, to diagnose dependencies and restore the delivered DMS services.

### Help Desk and Service-Request Management

WHO-designated users will report incidents and service requests through an agreed email or ticketing channel. Each request will receive a unique identifier and will be recorded with its category, severity, affected environment, reported time, owner, status, actions taken and closure evidence. Argusoft will acknowledge, triage, classify, assign, investigate, resolve, test and close each request in coordination with the authorized WHO representative. Duplicate requests will be linked, material status changes will be communicated, unresolved issues will follow the agreed escalation path, and closure will require confirmation of resolution or an agreed disposition. A request may be reopened if the issue persists, and recurring solutions will be incorporated into the knowledge base and known-error records.

### Support Window, Severity and Escalation

The 8×5 application-support window will provide agreed overlap with WHO Geneva/CET business hours. The exact service window, authorized contacts, holiday calendar and escalation arrangements will be confirmed during inception and recorded in the Support and Maintenance Plan.

As a provisional baseline, Critical incidents—such as Production unavailability, data corruption, a major security exposure or a critical process blocked without a workaround—will receive an initial response within one business hour. High-severity incidents affecting a major function without an acceptable workaround will receive an initial response within four business hours. Medium-severity incidents for which a reasonable workaround exists will receive an initial response within one business day, and Low-severity usability, presentation, documentation or non-urgent requests will receive an initial response within two business days. Resolution or workaround targets will depend on diagnosis, impact and complexity. Final definitions, response targets, escalation thresholds and resolution expectations will be agreed with WHO during inception.

### Automated Monitoring and Operational Response

Argusoft will configure 24×7 automated monitoring and alert generation for application and API availability, infrastructure health and utilization, database availability and capacity, failed deployments, failed or delayed background jobs, DMS–xMart integration failures, error rates and application exceptions, authentication and authorization failures, certificate expiration, backup success or failure, security events and significant configuration changes. The 24×7 commitment relates to automated monitoring and alert generation; human investigation and intervention will follow the agreed 8×5 support and escalation model unless otherwise agreed with WHO.

Incidents will be managed through triage, containment, workaround or service restoration, permanent correction, regression testing and closure confirmation. Recurring or significant incidents will be handled through problem management, including root-cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions and knowledge-base updates. Root-Cause Analysis reports will be provided for Critical incidents and for other incidents requested by WHO.

### Controlled Change, Release and Security Maintenance

Application fixes, minor modifications and infrastructure changes will follow controlled change and release procedures, including impact assessment, WHO prioritization where applicable, source control, peer review, testing in the appropriate environment, approval, deployment through CI/CD or Infrastructure-as-Code pipelines, rollback planning and post-deployment verification. Emergency changes will be documented and retrospectively reviewed.

Argusoft’s development, DevOps and in-house cybersecurity teams will support vulnerability triage, dependency and platform patching, security-event investigation, remediation and verification throughout the warranty. Critical and High-severity security findings attributable to the delivered solution will be remediated before warranty closure. Security updates will be impact-assessed, tested and deployed through WHO-approved change procedures, and their status will be included in the monthly report.

### Backup, Recovery and Service Continuity

Argusoft will monitor configured backup processes, support periodic restoration verification, maintain recovery and rollback procedures, and assist in restoring application services following an operational failure. Support will include failed-job restart and retry, deployment rollback and configuration recovery using approved operational runbooks. Backup retention, restoration frequency and recovery objectives will be agreed with WHO based on the approved Azure architecture and applicable WHO policies.

### Reporting and Governance

Argusoft will submit a Monthly Support and Maintenance Report covering incidents and service requests opened, closed and outstanding; severity and response performance; root-cause analyses and recurring problems; application fixes and minor modifications; infrastructure and configuration changes; deployments and rollbacks; monitoring availability and significant alerts; capacity and performance observations; backup and restoration status; certificate status; security vulnerabilities, patches and remediation; DMS–xMart integration issues; risks and dependencies; recommended actions; and planned activities for the next period. Review meetings and escalation discussions will be held with WHO as agreed to prioritize work and maintain operational transparency.

### Warranty Completion and Acceptance

At the end of the warranty period, Argusoft will submit a Warranty Completion Report consolidating incidents, defects, minor modifications, releases, infrastructure changes, monitoring results, security remediation, open-item status and operational recommendations. Warranty completion will be subject to WHO working-group review and confirmation that all agreed Critical and High-severity warranty issues have been resolved and that any remaining lower-severity items have an agreed disposition.

Most significantly, our solutions are incredibly protean, ensuring that the business needs are always quickly and easily aligned to the solution.  We capitalize on our low-code framework to deliver fully customized solutions that are very stable, quick to configure and hence faster to deliver.


Argonauts (team argusoft\!) are trained to think **‘design’** at every step.  We architect, design, and code, always keeping our clients' business objectives in mind.  We work as total partners, fully shouldering the responsibility of their business enabling software systems or, in the case of software product companies, as trusted technology partners of their core business offering.

Argusoft’s forte is its solution design and technological prowess to build and deploy large enterprise-class software systems successfully.  Several of these systems have also been developed and managed by Argusoft for several years. Argusoft has never been restricted by domains or verticals.

# Annexure 4 – Functional Compliance Matrix (Uc001–Uc061) {#annexure-4-–-functional-compliance-matrix-(uc001–uc061)}

**Introduction**

This Functional Compliance Matrix provides a use-case-level mapping of Argusoft's proposed solution against the Functional Requirements for the Health Accounts Data System (DMS), including all use cases **UC001–UC061 and UC060.1**.

Argusoft confirms that the proposed solution is designed to fulfil the functional requirements defined in the WHO Functional Requirements document. The implementation will follow the phased approach specified by WHO, with the functionalities identified for the Pilot delivered first and the remaining functionalities incorporated progressively following Pilot approval. The Pilot list has been considered in accordance with the clarification issued by WHO, including the clarification that general dashboard functionality is included in the Pilot.

* **Phase 1 – Pilot:**  
  Functional requirements identified by WHO for delivery as part of the Pilot implementation. This includes the Pilot functionalities specified in the WHO Functional Requirements document and the subsequent clarification that **general dashboard functionality is included in the Pilot**.  
* **Phase 2 – Post-Pilot:**  
  Remaining functional requirements that will be delivered progressively following successful completion and approval of the Pilot, in accordance with the phased implementation approach agreed with WHO.

UC001–UC061 Functional Compliance Matrix

| UC | Functional Requirement | Delivery Stage | Proposed Response |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| UC001 | Web Based Application | **Pilot** | DMS will be delivered as a browser-based web application accessible without client-side installation. |
| UC002 | Access to All Modules from Application Home Site | **Pilot** | A centralized DMS home site will provide access to all modules according to user permissions. |
| UC003 | Dashboard Displayed in Application Home Site | **Pilot** | A DMS dashboard will be provided on the application home site, with detailed dashboard content finalized with WHO during inception. |
| UC003.1 | Different Dashboard for Administrators and Regular Users | **Post-Pilot** | Role-specific dashboard views will be supported and configured according to user roles and permissions. |
| UC004 | Users Module | **Pilot** | User administration, access management, role assignment and user status management will be provided. |
| UC005 | Grant Access for a User | **Pilot** | Administrators will be able to grant DMS access to authorized users. |
| UC006 | Access with WHO Single Sign-On | **Pilot** | DMS will integrate with WHO Entra ID/Single Sign-On for authenticated access. |
| UC007 | Assign Roles to DMS Users | **Pilot** | Administrators will be able to assign roles and associated permissions to DMS users. |
| UC008 | Edit DMS Roles Permissions | **Post-Pilot** | Authorized administrators will be able to configure and manage permissions associated with DMS roles. |
| UC009 | Restrict Countries for a Regular User | **Post-Pilot** | Country-level access restrictions will be supported for Regular Users according to assigned permissions. |
| UC010 | Temporarily Disable a DMS User | **Post-Pilot** | Administrators will be able to temporarily disable a user's DMS access. |
| UC011 | Enable a Disabled DMS User | **Post-Pilot** | Administrators will be able to restore access for previously disabled users. |
| UC012 | DMS Users Cannot Be Deleted | **Pilot** | User records will be retained, with access managed through user status rather than deletion. |
| UC013 | Setup Module | **Pilot** | A centralized Setup and Configuration module will manage DMS configuration components. |
| UC014 | Import Configuration Data from xMart | **Pilot** | Required configuration data will be retrieved/imported from xMart through the agreed integration mechanisms. |
| UC015 | Reorder Columns in All Data Components Lists | **Pilot** | Applicable data-component lists will support configurable column ordering. |
| UC016 | Edit Predefined List of Values | **Pilot** | Authorized administrators will be able to manage predefined configuration values. |
| UC017 | Create a New Value for a Data Component | **Pilot** | Authorized users will be able to create new configuration values for applicable data components. |
| UC018 | Create New Attributes for Existing Data Components | **Post-Pilot** | The configuration model will support creation of additional attributes for applicable data components. |
| UC019 | Edit the Details of a Component | **Post-Pilot** | Authorized users will be able to edit applicable component details through the Setup module. |
| UC020 | Delete One Value of a Component | **Post-Pilot** | Authorized administrators will be able to remove applicable configuration values subject to data dependencies. |
| UC021 | Export and Import Data Components Values and Their Attributes | **Post-Pilot** | Applicable configuration values and attributes will support import and export. |
| UC022 | Groups of Countries | **Pilot** | Country groups will be supported for configuration, access, calculations, quality checks and reporting. |
| UC023 | Countries Data Reporting Follow Up | **Pilot** | Country/year reporting status and follow-up information will be supported. |
| UC024 | Data Publishing Status Flag | **Pilot** | Data publishing/readiness status will be maintained and displayed within DMS. |
| UC025 | Predefined Crosses | **Pilot** | Predefined classification crosses will be available and manageable by authorized users. |
| UC026 | Custom Crosses | **Pilot** | Users will be able to create applicable country-specific/custom classification crosses. |
| UC027 | Metadata Fields for Each Observation | **Pilot** | Observation-level metadata will be supported, including applicable legacy formula metadata. |
| UC028 | Access Metadata Files Stored in SharePoint from DMS | **Pilot** | DMS will provide access to applicable metadata files stored through the agreed WHO SharePoint/xMart arrangement. |
| UC029 | Predefined Formulas | **Pilot** | A formula management and calculation capability will support predefined indicator formulas. |
| UC030 | Custom Formulas | **Pilot** | Authorized users will be able to create and use custom formulas according to applicable permissions. |
| UC031 | Workbooks Module | **Pilot** | The Workbook module will provide Excel-like data viewing/editing, formulas, metadata and data manipulation capabilities. |
| UC031.1 | Order Workbook Data Based on Any Element Displayed | **Post-Pilot** | Workbook data will support applicable sorting and ordering based on displayed elements. |
| UC032 | Export Workbooks Data | **Post-Pilot** | Workbook data will be exportable using the supported formats and templates. |
| UC033 | Locking Functionality | **Post-Pilot** | Workbook-level locking will prevent simultaneous conflicting edits to the same data. |
| UC034 | User Customized Display of Metadata Fields | **Post-Pilot** | Users will be able to customize the display of applicable metadata fields. |
| UC035 | Reports Module | **Pilot** | A dedicated Reports and Analytics module will provide predefined and configurable reporting capabilities. |
| UC036 | Create and Edit a Predefined Report Available to All Users | **Pilot** | Authorized administrators will be able to create and edit predefined reports available to users. |
| UC037 | Create and Edit Customized Reports Available for the User Only | **Post-Pilot** | Users will be able to create and manage customized reports for their own use. |
| UC038 | Copy a Report as the Basis for a New Report | **Post-Pilot** | Existing reports will be copyable and usable as the basis for new reports. |
| UC039 | Data Tracking Reports | **Pilot** | Data tracking and reporting capabilities will support monitoring of data status and changes. |
| UC040 | User Customized List of Reports | **Post-Pilot** | Users will be able to manage their personalized list of applicable reports. |
| UC041 | Multilanguage Report | **Post-Pilot** | Reports will support applicable WHO official-language labels and multilingual reporting requirements. |
| UC042 | Export Report to Excel Format | **Pilot** | Reports will support export to Excel format. |
| UC043 | Variables, Data Sets and Metadata Versioning | **Pilot** | Version history for applicable observations, variables, datasets and metadata will be supported through xMart/DMS integration. |
| UC044 | Compare and Restore Previous Versions | **Pilot** | Authorized users will be able to compare and restore applicable previous versions. |
| UC045 | API from xMart to DMS | **Pilot** | DMS will retrieve required data from xMart through the defined API integration. |
| UC046 | API from DMS to xMart – Data and Metadata Updates | **Pilot** | DMS changes will be transmitted to xMart through the agreed API integration. |
| UC047 | Quality Checks Module | **Pilot** | A dedicated Quality Checks module will support rule management, execution and result visualization. |
| UC048 | Exclude Countries from a Quality Check | **Pilot** | Quality-check execution will support country/group exclusions. |
| UC049 | Create and Edit a Predefined Quality Check Rule Available to All Users | **Post-Pilot** | Authorized administrators will be able to create and edit predefined quality-check rules. |
| UC050 | Create and Edit a Customized Quality Check Rule Available for the User | **Pilot** | Users will be able to create and manage customized quality-check rules according to permissions. |
| UC051 | Export and Import Quality Checks Rules | **Post-Pilot** | Quality-check rule configurations will support import and export. |
| UC052 | Manual Run of Quality Check from a Workbook | **Pilot** | Users will be able to manually trigger applicable quality checks from the Workbook context. |
| UC053 | Predefined Quality Checks During Development | **Pilot** | Predefined quality-check rules will be incorporated based on WHO requirements. |
| UC054 | Configuration Values for Quality Check Rules | **Pilot** | Quality-check thresholds and configuration values will be configurable. |
| UC055 | Generate, Visualize and Download Quality Check Report | **Pilot** | Quality-check results will be generated, visualized and downloadable through DMS. |
| UC056 | Develop Functionalities in WHO xMart | **Pilot** | Argusoft will work with WHO to implement the required xMart-side functionality/configuration necessary to fulfil the agreed DMS scope. |
| UC057 | Expected Processing Volumes | **Post-Pilot** | The solution architecture will support the specified data volumes and year-end processing requirements. |
| UC058 | Notifications Module | **Post-Pilot** | An event-based In-App Notifications module will be provided. |
| UC059 | Create or Edit Notifications | **Post-Pilot** | Authorized administrators will be able to create and edit notification definitions and targeting. |
| UC060 | Old DMS Formulas Migration | **Pilot** | Argusoft will perform the required one-off migration of legacy DMS formulas into xMart as metadata and make them accessible through the new DMS. |
| UC060.1 | Translation of Old DMS Formulas into New DMS Syntax | **Post-Pilot** | Argusoft will translate legacy formulas into the new DMS formula syntax as part of the agreed migration scope. |
| UC061 | Phased Implementation | **Pilot** | Implementation will follow the WHO-defined Pilot and subsequent Post-Pilot delivery approach. |
